question: Which among the following international boundaries is the longest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The international border between India and Bangladesh is currently considered the longest land border between two countries. It spans approximately 4,096 kilometers (2,545 miles) in length.**
 
• The border between** India and Bangladesh** is a complex and diverse boundary that runs across various states and regions, and it is an important aspect of the bilateral relations between the two countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The international border between India and Myanmar (formerly known as Burma) is approximately 1,643 kilometers (1,020 miles) in length.**

 
 
• It stretches from the tri-junction of India,** Myanmar, and Bangladesh in the east to the tri-junction of India, Myanmar, and China in the north.**
 
• The border runs through the northeastern states of India, including **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.**
 
• It is an important border for trade, cultural exchanges, and regional cooperation between India and Myanmar.
 
 
 
• **The international border between India and China, often referred to as the Line of Actual Control (LAC), stretches approximately 3,488 kilometers (2,167 miles) in length.**
 
 
• It spans from the easternmost point of the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir in the west to the tri-junction of India, China, and Myanmar in the east.
 
• The border passes through various regions, including Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The Indo-China border is a disputed boundary, and both countries have experienced tensions and conflicts along certain sectors of the border over the years.
 
 
 
• **The international border between India and Pakistan, known as the Line of Control (LoC), spans approximately 2,300 kilometers (1,430 miles)**.
 
 
• It runs from the northernmost point of India in the state of Jammu and Kashmir, extends westward across the states of Punjab and Rajasthan, and ends at the Arabian Sea in the state of Gujarat.
 
• The Indo-Pak border is a heavily guarded and sensitive boundary due to the historical and ongoing conflicts between the two countries.
 
• It is monitored and patrolled by security forces from both India and Pakistan.
